ai_en: Jo pulled a pencil from her pocket and dashed off a hasty sketch of the room on the back of an old envelope.
It was a jolly little supper, with the sisters' laughter ringing round the table.
Amy's eyes were full of tears, and she declared she would never speak of her pears again.
The small store of things they had seemed to satisfy their simple wants.
Jo leaned her chin on her hand and lay staring at the fire, lost in a pleasant dream.
She resolved firmly that she would do better next time.
She put her whole soul into the little song.
Amy curled up on the sofa with a book and a dish of bonbons.
Mr. Brooke was a quiet young man, not handsome, but kind and steady.
